The Cyber Regulations Advisory Committee shall consist of a Chairperson and such number of other official and non-official members representing the interests principally affected or having special knowledge of the subject-matter as the Central Government may deem fit. The Cyber Regulations Advisory Committee shall advise— (a) the Central Government either generally as regards any rules or for any other purpose connected with this Act; (b) the Controller in framing the regulations under this Act.
plain_english_summary: The Central Government must constitute the Cyber Regulations Advisory Committee to advise the Central Government on rules under the Act and the Controller on framing regulations.

properties.regulation_type: Cyber Regulations Advisory Committee
Cyber Regulations Advisory Committee
Cyber Regulations Advisory Committee

title: Documents or Transactions Excluded from the Act
clause_text: Documents or transactions to which the Act shall not apply: 1. A negotiable instrument (other than a cheque) as defined in section 13 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881. 2. A power-of-attorney as defined in section 1A of the Powers-of-Attorney Act, 1882. 3. A trust as defined in section 3 of the Indian Trust Act, 1882. 4. A will as defined in clause (h) of section 2 of the Indian Succession Act, 1925, including any other testamentary disposition by whatever name called. 5. Any contract for the sale or conveyance of immovable property or any interest in such property.
plain_english_summary: The First Schedule lists documents and transactions excluded from the Act: negotiable instruments (other than cheques), powers of attorney, trusts, wills and testamentary dispositions, and contracts for sale or conveyance of immovable property.

title: Compounding of Offences
clause_text: A court of competent jurisdiction may compound offences, other than offences for which the punishment for life or imprisonment for a term exceeding three years has been provided, under this Act: Provided that the court shall not compound such offence where the accused is, by reason of his previous conviction, liable to either enhanced punishment or to a punishment of a different kind: Provided further that the court shall not compound any offence where such offence affects the socio economic conditions of the country or has been committed against a child below the age of 18 years or a woman.
plain_english_summary: A court may compound offences under the Act except those carrying life imprisonment or imprisonment exceeding three years, or where the accused has a prior conviction attracting enhanced punishment, or the offence affects socio-economic conditions or is against a child or woman.

title: Bailable and Cognizable Offences
clause_text: Notwithstanding anything contained in the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, the offence punishable with imprisonment of three years and above shall be cognizable and the offence punishable with imprisonment of three years shall be bailable.
plain_english_summary: Offences punishable with imprisonment of three years or more are cognizable. Offences punishable with exactly three years are bailable, notwithstanding the CrPC.

title: Power to Investigate Offences
clause_text: Notwithstanding anything contained in the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, a police officer not below the rank of Inspector shall investigate any offence under this Act.
plain_english_summary: Only a police officer of Inspector rank or above may investigate offences under the Act, notwithstanding the CrPC.

title: Compounding of Contraventions
clause_text: Any contravention under this Act may, either before or after the institution of adjudication proceedings, be compounded by the Controller or such other officer as may be specially authorised by him in this behalf or by the adjudicating officer, as the case may be, subject to such conditions as the Controller or such other officer or the adjudicating officer may specify: Provided that such sum shall not, in any case, exceed the maximum amount of the penalty which may be imposed under this Act for the contravention so compounded.
plain_english_summary: Contraventions under the Act may be compounded by the Controller or adjudicating officer before or after adjudication proceedings begin, subject to conditions and a cap at the maximum penalty for the contravention. A person cannot have a contravention compounded twice within three years.

properties.regulation_type: Compounding of Contraventions
Compounding of Contraventions

title: Recovery of Penalty or Compensation
clause_text: A penalty imposed or compensation awarded under this Act, if it is not paid, shall be recovered as an arrear of land revenue and the licence or the electronic signature Certificate, as the case may be, shall be suspended till the penalty is paid.
plain_english_summary: Unpaid penalties or compensation under the Act are recoverable as arrears of land revenue, and the relevant licence or electronic signature certificate is suspended until payment is made.

title: Definition - Affixing Electronic Signature
clause_text: "affixing electronic signature" with its grammatical variations and cognate expressions means adoption of any methodology or procedure by a person for the purpose of authenticating an electronic record by means of digital signature.
plain_english_summary: Affixing an electronic signature means adopting any method or procedure to authenticate an electronic record using a digital signature.

title: Definition - Appropriate Government
clause_text: "appropriate Government" means as respects any matter,— (i) enumerated in List II of the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution; (ii) relating to any State law enacted under List III of the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution, the State Government and in any other case, the Central Government.
plain_english_summary: Appropriate Government means the State Government for matters under List II (State List) or List III (Concurrent List) of the Constitution, and the Central Government in all other cases.

title: Definition - Asymmetric Crypto System
clause_text: "asymmetric crypto system" means a system of a secure key pair consisting of a private key for creating a digital signature and a public key to verify the digital signature.
plain_english_summary: An asymmetric crypto system is a cryptographic key pair where a private key creates a digital signature and the corresponding public key verifies it.

title: Definition - Certification Practice Statement
clause_text: "certification practice statement" means a statement issued by a Certifying Authority to specify the practices that the Certifying Authority employs in issuing electronic signature Certificates.
plain_english_summary: A certification practice statement is a document issued by a Certifying Authority setting out the practices it uses when issuing electronic signature certificates.

title: Definition - Computer System
clause_text: "computer system" means a device or collection of devices, including input and output support devices and excluding calculators which are not programmable and capable of being used in conjunction with external files, which contain computer programmes, electronic instructions, input data and output data, that performs logic, arithmetic, data storage and retrieval, communication control and other functions.
plain_english_summary: A computer system is a programmable device or collection of devices that processes logic, arithmetic, data storage, retrieval, and communication functions, including input/output devices but excluding non-programmable calculators.

title: Definition - Digital Signature Certificate
clause_text: "Digital Signature Certificate" means a Digital Signature Certificate issued under sub-section (4) of section 35.
plain_english_summary: A Digital Signature Certificate is a certificate issued by a Certifying Authority under section 35(4) that validates the subscriber's public key.

title: Definition - Electronic Gazette
clause_text: "Electronic Gazette" means the Official Gazette published in the electronic form.
plain_english_summary: The Electronic Gazette is the Official Gazette published in electronic form.

title: Definition - Electronic Signature Certificate
clause_text: "Electronic Signature Certificate" means an Electronic Signature Certificate issued under section 35 and includes Digital Signature Certificate.
plain_english_summary: An Electronic Signature Certificate is a certificate issued under section 35 that includes Digital Signature Certificates.

title: Definition - Key Pair
clause_text: "key pair", in an asymmetric crypto system, means a private key and its mathematically related public key, which are so related that the public key can verify a digital signature created by the private key.
plain_english_summary: A key pair consists of a mathematically related private key and public key, where the public key can verify digital signatures created by the private key.

title: Definition - Private Key
clause_text: "private key" means the key of a key pair used to create a digital signature.
plain_english_summary: A private key is the key in a key pair used to create a digital signature.

title: Definition - Public Key
clause_text: "public key" means the key of a key pair used to verify a digital signature and listed in the Digital Signature Certificate.
plain_english_summary: A public key is the key in a key pair used to verify a digital signature, and it is listed in the Digital Signature Certificate.

title: Definition - Security Procedure
clause_text: "security procedure" means the security procedure prescribed under section 16 by the Central Government.
plain_english_summary: Security procedure means the procedure prescribed by the Central Government under section 16 for securing electronic records and signatures.

title: Definition - Verify
clause_text: "verify", in relation to a digital signature, electronic record or public key, with its grammatical variations and cognate expressions, means to determine whether— (a) the initial electronic record was affixed with the digital signature by the use of private key corresponding to the public key of the subscriber; (b) the initial electronic record is retained intact or has been altered since such electronic record was so affixed with the digital signature.
plain_english_summary: To verify a digital signature means to determine that the electronic record was signed using the subscriber's private key and that the record has not been altered since it was signed.

title: Cross-Reference Interpretation
clause_text: Any reference in this Act to any enactment or any provision thereof shall, in relation to an area in which such enactment or such provision is not in force, be construed as a reference to the corresponding law or the relevant provision of the corresponding law, if any, in force in that area.
plain_english_summary: Any reference in the Act to a law or provision not in force in a particular area shall be read as a reference to the corresponding law or provision that is in force in that area.

title: Use of Electronic Records in Government - Rule-Making
clause_text: The appropriate Government may, for the purposes of sub-section (1), by rules, prescribe— (a) the manner and format in which such electronic records shall be filed, created or issued; (b) the manner or method of payment of any fee or charges for filing, creation or issue any electronic record under clause (a).
plain_english_summary: The appropriate Government may make rules prescribing the manner, format, and method of payment for electronic filing, creation, or issuance of records under section 6(1).

properties.regulation_type: Use of Electronic Records in Government - Rule-Making

title: Power to Make Rules on Electronic Signature
clause_text: The Central Government may, for the purposes of this Act, by rules, prescribe— (a) the type of electronic signature; (b) the manner and format in which the electronic signature shall be affixed; (c) the manner or procedure which facilitates identification of the person affixing the electronic signature; (d) control processes and procedures to ensure adequate integrity, security and confidentiality of electronic records or payments; and (e) any other matter which is necessary to give legal effect to electronic signatures.
plain_english_summary: The Central Government may make rules covering the type, manner, and format of electronic signatures, procedures for identifying the signatory, and controls to ensure integrity and security of electronic records.

properties.regulation_type: Power to Make Rules on Electronic Signature

title: Acknowledgment - No Stipulation and Reasonable Time
clause_text: Where the originator has not stipulated that the electronic record shall be binding only on receipt of such acknowledgment, and the acknowledgment has not been received by the originator within the time specified or agreed or, if no time has been specified or agreed to within a reasonable time, then the originator may give notice to the addressee stating that no acknowledgment has been received by him and specifying a reasonable time by which the acknowledgment must be received by him and if no acknowledgment is received within the aforesaid time limit he may after giving notice to the addressee, treat the electronic record as though it has never been sent.
plain_english_summary: Where the originator has not made binding effect conditional on acknowledgment but none has arrived within the stipulated or reasonable time, the originator may give notice and, if still no acknowledgment is received, treat the record as never sent.

properties.regulation_type: Acknowledgment - No Stipulation and Reasonable Time
Acknowledgment - No Stipulation and Reasonable Time

title: Place of Despatch and Receipt of Electronic Record
clause_text: Save as otherwise agreed to between the originator and the addressee, an electronic record is deemed to be despatched at the place where the originator has his place of business, and is deemed to be received at the place where the addressee has his place of business.
plain_english_summary: Unless agreed otherwise, an electronic record is deemed dispatched from the originator's place of business and received at the addressee's place of business.

properties.regulation_type: Place of Despatch and Receipt of Electronic Record
Place of Despatch and Receipt of Electronic Record

title: Application for Certifying Authority Licence
clause_text: Every application for issue of a licence shall be in such form as may be prescribed by the Central Government. Every application for issue of a licence shall be accompanied by— (a) a certification practice statement; (b) a statement including the procedures with respect to identification of the applicant; (c) payment of such fees, not exceeding twenty-five thousand rupees as may be prescribed by the Central Government; (d) such other documents, as may be prescribed by the Central Government.
plain_english_summary: An application for a Certifying Authority licence must be in the prescribed form, accompanied by a certification practice statement, identification procedures, a fee not exceeding Rs 25,000, and other prescribed documents.

properties.regulation_type: Application for Certifying Authority Licence
Application for Certifying Authority Licence

title: Renewal of Certifying Authority Licence
clause_text: An application for renewal of a licence shall be— (a) in such form; (b) accompanied by such fees, not exceeding five thousand rupees, as may be prescribed by the Central Government and shall be made not less than forty-five days before the date of expiry of the period of validity of the licence.
plain_english_summary: A licence renewal application must be submitted at least 45 days before expiry, in the prescribed form, with a fee not exceeding Rs 5,000.

properties.regulation_type: Renewal of Certifying Authority Licence

title: Procedure for Grant or Rejection of Licence
clause_text: The Controller may, on receipt of an application under sub-section (1) of section 21, after considering the documents accompanying the application and such other factors, as he deems fit, grant the licence or reject the application: Provided that no application shall be rejected under this section unless the applicant has been given a reasonable opportunity of presenting his case.
plain_english_summary: The Controller may grant or reject a Certifying Authority licence after considering accompanying documents and other relevant factors, but must give the applicant a reasonable opportunity to present their case before rejection.

properties.regulation_type: Procedure for Grant or Rejection of Licence

title: Notice of Suspension or Revocation of Certifying Authority Licence
clause_text: Where the licence of the Certifying Authority is suspended or revoked, the Controller shall publish notice of such suspension or revocation, as the case may be, in the data base maintained by him. Where one or more repositories are specified, the Controller shall publish notices of such suspension or revocation, as the case may be, in all such repositories: Provided that the data base containing the notice of such suspension or revocation, as the case may be, shall be made available through a web site which shall be accessible round the clock.
plain_english_summary: When a Certifying Authority licence is suspended or revoked, the Controller must publish notice in the relevant database and all specified repositories, accessible round the clock via a website.

properties.duty_nature: Notice of Suspension or Revocation of Certifying Authority Licence
Notice of Suspension or Revocation of Certifying Authority Licence

title: Power to Delegate
clause_text: The Controller may, in writing, authorise the Deputy Controller, Assistant Controller or any officer to exercise any of the powers of the Controller under this Chapter.
plain_english_summary: The Controller may delegate any of their powers under Chapter VI to the Deputy Controller, Assistant Controller, or any other officer, by written authorisation.

properties.regulation_type: Power to Delegate
Power to Delegate
Power to Delegate

title: Power to Investigate Contraventions
clause_text: The Controller or any officer authorised by him in this behalf shall take up for investigation any contravention of the provisions of this Act, rules or regulations made thereunder. The Controller or any officer authorised by him in this behalf shall exercise the like powers which are conferred on Income-tax authorities under Chapter XIII of the Income-tax Act, 1961, and shall exercise such powers, subject to such limitations laid down under that Act.
plain_english_summary: The Controller or an authorised officer may investigate contraventions of the Act and its rules, with powers equivalent to Income Tax authorities under Chapter XIII of the Income Tax Act, 1961.

properties.regulation_type: Power to Investigate Contraventions

title: Access to Computers and Data for Investigation
clause_text: Without prejudice to the provisions of sub-section (1) of section 69, the Controller or any person authorised by him shall, if he has reasonable cause to suspect that any contravention of the provisions of this Chapter has been committed, have access to any computer system, any apparatus, data or any other material connected with such system, for the purpose of searching or causing a search to be made for obtaining any information or data contained in or available to such computer system.
plain_english_summary: The Controller or an authorised person may access any computer system and data when there is reasonable cause to suspect a contravention of the Act, for the purpose of searching for relevant information.

properties.regulation_type: Access to Computers and Data for Investigation

title: Certifying Authority - Display of Licence
clause_text: Every Certifying Authority shall display its licence at a conspicuous place of the premises in which it carries on its business.
plain_english_summary: Every Certifying Authority must display its licence at a conspicuous place in its business premises.

properties.duty_nature: Certifying Authority - Display of Licence

title: Certifying Authority - Surrender of Licence
clause_text: Every Certifying Authority whose licence is suspended or revoked shall immediately after such suspension or revocation, surrender the licence to the Controller. Where any Certifying Authority fails to surrender a licence under sub-section (1), the person in whose favour a licence is issued, shall be guilty of an offence and shall be punished with imprisonment which may extend up to six months or a fine which may extend up to ten thousand rupees or with both.
plain_english_summary: A Certifying Authority whose licence is suspended or revoked must immediately surrender the licence to the Controller. Failure to do so is an offence punishable with imprisonment up to six months or a fine up to Rs 10,000, or both.

properties.duty_nature: Certifying Authority - Surrender of Licence
Certifying Authority - Surrender of Licence

title: Representations Upon Issuance of Digital Signature Certificate
clause_text: A Certifying Authority while issuing a Digital Signature Certificate shall certify that— (a) it has complied with the provisions of this Act and the rules and regulations made thereunder; (b) it has published the Digital Signature Certificate or otherwise made it available to such person relying on it and the subscriber has accepted it; (c) the subscriber holds the private key corresponding to the public key, listed in the Digital Signature Certificate; (ca) the subscriber holds a private key which is capable of creating a digital signature; (cb) the public key to be listed in the certificate can be used to verify a digital signature affixed by the private key held by the subscriber; (d) the subscriber's public key and private key constitute a functioning key pair; (e) the information contained in the Digital Signature Certificate is accurate; and (f) it has no knowledge of any material fact, which if included in the Digital Signature Certificate would adversely affect the reliability of the representations.
plain_english_summary: When issuing a Digital Signature Certificate, a Certifying Authority must certify compliance with the Act, accuracy of information, that the subscriber holds the correct private key capable of creating digital signatures, that the key pair functions correctly, and absence of knowledge of any adverse material fact.

properties.duty_nature: Representations Upon Issuance of Digital Signature Certificate
Representations Upon Issuance of Digital Signature Certificate

title: Notice of Suspension or Revocation of Digital Signature Certificate
clause_text: Where a Digital Signature Certificate is suspended or revoked under section 37 or section 38, the Certifying Authority shall publish a notice of such suspension or revocation, as the case may be, in the repository specified in the Digital Signature Certificate for publication of such notice. Where one or more repositories are specified, the Certifying Authority shall publish notices of such suspension or revocation, as the case may be, in all such repositories.
plain_english_summary: When a Digital Signature Certificate is suspended or revoked, the Certifying Authority must publish notice of the suspension or revocation in all repositories specified in the certificate.

properties.duty_nature: Notice of Suspension or Revocation of Digital Signature Certificate

title: Duties of Subscriber of Electronic Signature Certificate
clause_text: In respect of Electronic Signature Certificate the subscriber shall perform such duties as may be prescribed.
plain_english_summary: A subscriber holding an Electronic Signature Certificate must perform such duties as are prescribed by the Central Government.

properties.duty_nature: Duties of Subscriber of Electronic Signature Certificate

title: Acceptance of Digital Signature Certificate
clause_text: A subscriber shall be deemed to have accepted a Digital Signature Certificate if he publishes or authorises the publication of a Digital Signature Certificate— (a) to one or more persons; (b) in a repository; or otherwise demonstrates his approval of the Digital Signature Certificate in any manner. By accepting a Digital Signature Certificate the subscriber certifies to all who reasonably rely on the information contained in the Digital Signature Certificate that— (a) the subscriber holds the private key corresponding to the public key listed in the Digital Signature Certificate and is entitled to hold the same; (b) all representations made by the subscriber to the Certifying Authority and all material relevant to the information contained in the Digital Signature Certificate are true; (c) all information in the Digital Signature Certificate that is within the knowledge of the subscriber is true.
plain_english_summary: A subscriber is deemed to have accepted a Digital Signature Certificate by publishing it or otherwise demonstrating approval, and in doing so certifies the accuracy of all information in it to anyone relying on it.

properties.duty_nature: Acceptance of Digital Signature Certificate
Acceptance of Digital Signature Certificate

title: Adjudication - Inquiry and Imposition of Penalty
clause_text: The adjudicating officer shall, after giving the person referred to in sub-section (1) a reasonable opportunity for making representation in the matter and if, on such inquiry, he is satisfied that the person has committed the contravention, he may impose such penalty or award such compensation as he thinks fit in accordance with the provisions of that section.
plain_english_summary: The adjudicating officer must give the accused a reasonable opportunity to make representations before imposing any penalty or awarding compensation.

properties.regulation_type: Adjudication - Inquiry and Imposition of Penalty

title: Adjudicating Officer - Civil Court Powers
clause_text: Every adjudicating officer shall have the powers of a civil court which are conferred on the Appellate Tribunal under sub-section (2) of section 58, and— (a) all proceedings before it shall be deemed to be judicial proceedings within the meaning of sections 193 and 228 of the Indian Penal Code; (b) shall be deemed to be a civil court for the purposes of sections 345 and 346 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973; (c) shall be deemed to be a civil court for purposes of Order XXI of the Civil Procedure Code, 1908.
plain_english_summary: An adjudicating officer has civil court powers including those under the CPC, and proceedings before them are deemed judicial proceedings under the IPC and CrPC.

properties.regulation_type: Adjudicating Officer - Civil Court Powers

title: Decision by Majority in Appellate Tribunal
clause_text: If the Members of a Bench consisting of two Members differ in opinion on any point, they shall state the point or points on which they differ, and make a reference to the Chairperson of the Appellate Tribunal who shall hear the point or points himself and such point or points shall be decided according to the opinion of the majority of the Members who have heard the case, including those who first heard it.
plain_english_summary: Where two members of a bench disagree, the disputed point is referred to the Chairperson and decided by the majority of all members who have heard the case.

properties.regulation_type: Decision by Majority in Appellate Tribunal

title: Orders Constituting Appellate Tribunal - Finality
clause_text: No order of the Central Government appointing any person as the Chairperson or the Member of a Appellate Tribunal shall be called in question in any manner and no act or proceeding before a Appellate Tribunal shall be called in question in any manner on the ground merely of any defect in the constitution of a Appellate Tribunal.
plain_english_summary: Appointments to the Appellate Tribunal cannot be challenged, and acts or proceedings of the Tribunal cannot be invalidated merely due to a defect in its constitution.

properties.regulation_type: Orders Constituting Appellate Tribunal - Finality
Orders Constituting Appellate Tribunal - Finality

title: Appeal - Powers of Appellate Tribunal on Hearing
clause_text: On receipt of an appeal under sub-section (1), the Appellate Tribunal may, after giving the parties to the appeal, an opportunity of being heard, pass such orders thereon as it thinks fit, confirming, modifying or setting aside the order appealed against.
plain_english_summary: On receiving an appeal, the Appellate Tribunal may, after hearing the parties, confirm, modify, or set aside the order under appeal.

properties.regulation_type: Appeal - Powers of Appellate Tribunal on Hearing

title: Appeal - Expeditious Disposal
clause_text: The appeal filed before the Appellate Tribunal under sub-section (1) shall be dealt with by it as expeditiously as possible and endeavour shall be made by it to dispose of the appeal finally within six months from the date of receipt of the appeal.
plain_english_summary: The Appellate Tribunal must deal with appeals as expeditiously as possible and endeavour to dispose of them within six months of receipt.

properties.regulation_type: Appeal - Expeditious Disposal

title: Appellate Tribunal - Procedure and Natural Justice
clause_text: The Appellate Tribunal shall not be bound by the procedure laid down by the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 but shall be guided by the principles of natural justice and, subject to the other provisions of this Act and of any rules, the Appellate Tribunal shall have powers to regulate its own procedure including the place at which it shall have its sittings.
plain_english_summary: The Appellate Tribunal is not bound by the CPC but must be guided by the principles of natural justice and may regulate its own procedure, including the place of sittings.

properties.regulation_type: Appellate Tribunal - Procedure and Natural Justice

title: Right to Legal Representation Before Appellate Tribunal
clause_text: The appellant may either appear in person or authorise one or more legal practitioners or any of its officers to present his or its case before the Appellate Tribunal.
plain_english_summary: An appellant may appear in person or be represented by one or more legal practitioners or company officers before the Appellate Tribunal.

properties.right_nature: Right to Legal Representation Before Appellate Tribunal

title: Limitation for Appeals to Appellate Tribunal
clause_text: The provisions of the Limitation Act, 1963, shall, as far as may be, apply to an appeal made to the Appellate Tribunal.
plain_english_summary: The Limitation Act, 1963 applies, as far as practicable, to appeals made to the Appellate Tribunal.

properties.regulation_type: Limitation for Appeals to Appellate Tribunal

title: Punishment for Sending Offensive Messages [Struck Down]
clause_text: Any person who sends, by means of a computer resource or a communication device,— (a) any information that is grossly offensive or has menacing character; or (b) any information which he knows to be false, but for the purpose of causing annoyance, inconvenience, danger, obstruction, insult, injury, criminal intimidation, enmity, hatred or ill will, persistently by making use of such computer resource or a communication device; (c) any electronic mail or electronic mail message for the purpose of causing annoyance or inconvenience or to deceive or to mislead the addressee or recipient about the origin of such messages, shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and with fine.
plain_english_summary: Section 66A penalised sending grossly offensive, menacing, or false messages through computer resources or communication devices. This section was struck down by the Supreme Court of India in Shreya Singhal v. Union of India (2015) as unconstitutional.

title: Power of Controller to Give Directions
clause_text: The Controller may, by order, direct a Certifying Authority or any employee of such Authority to take such measures or cease carrying on such activities as specified in the order if those are necessary to ensure compliance with the provisions of this Act, rules or any regulations made thereunder. Any person who intentionally or knowingly fails to comply with any order under sub-section (1) shall be guilty of an offence and shall be liable on conviction to imprisonment for a term not exceeding two years or a fine not exceeding one lakh rupees or with both.
plain_english_summary: The Controller may direct a Certifying Authority or its employees to take action or stop activities to ensure compliance. Intentional non-compliance is an offence punishable with imprisonment up to two years or a fine up to Rs 1 lakh, or both.

properties.regulation_type: Power of Controller to Give Directions
Power of Controller to Give Directions

title: Interception and Monitoring - Safeguards
clause_text: The procedure and safeguards subject to which such interception or monitoring or decryption may be carried out, shall be such as may be prescribed.
plain_english_summary: The procedure and safeguards for interception, monitoring, or decryption of information must be prescribed by the Central Government.

properties.regulation_type: Interception and Monitoring - Safeguards

title: Failure to Assist Interception - Penalty
clause_text: The subscriber or intermediary or any person who fails to assist the agency referred to in sub-section (3) shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to seven years and shall also be liable to fine.
plain_english_summary: Any subscriber, intermediary, or person who fails to assist an authorised government agency with interception, monitoring, or decryption is punishable with imprisonment up to seven years and a fine.

title: Blocking of Information - Safeguards
clause_text: The procedure and safeguards subject to which such blocking for access by the public may be carried out, shall be such as may be prescribed.
plain_english_summary: The procedure and safeguards for blocking public access to information under section 69A must be prescribed by the Central Government.

properties.regulation_type: Blocking of Information - Safeguards

title: Blocking of Information - Penalty for Non-Compliance
clause_text: The intermediary who fails to comply with the direction issued under sub-section (1) shall be punished with an imprisonment for a term which may extend to seven years and also be liable to fine.
plain_english_summary: An intermediary that fails to comply with a blocking direction under section 69A(1) is punishable with imprisonment up to seven years and a fine.

title: Traffic Data Monitoring - Penalty for Non-Compliance
clause_text: Any intermediary who intentionally or knowingly contravenes the provisions of sub-section (2) shall be punished with an imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine.
plain_english_summary: An intermediary that intentionally or knowingly fails to provide technical assistance for traffic data monitoring under section 69B(2) is punishable with imprisonment up to three years and a fine.

title: Protected System - Authorisation of Access
clause_text: The appropriate Government may, by order in writing, authorise the persons who are authorised to access protected systems notified under sub-section (1).
plain_english_summary: The appropriate Government may by written order authorise specific persons to access protected computer systems.

properties.regulation_type: Protected System - Authorisation of Access

title: Protected System - Information Security Practices
clause_text: The Central Government shall prescribe the information security practices and procedures for such protected system.
plain_english_summary: The Central Government must prescribe information security practices and procedures specifically applicable to protected systems.

properties.duty_nature: Protected System - Information Security Practices

title: CERT-In Functions
clause_text: The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team shall serve as the national agency for performing the following functions in the area of cyber security,— (a) collection, analysis and dissemination of information on cyber incidents; (b) forecast and alerts of cyber security incidents; (c) emergency measures for handling cyber security incidents; (d) coordination of cyber incidents response activities; (e) issue guidelines, advisories, vulnerability notes and white papers relating to information security practices, procedures, prevention, response and reporting of cyber incidents; (f) such other functions relating to cyber security as may be prescribed.
plain_english_summary: CERT-In's statutory functions include collecting and analysing cyber incident data, issuing alerts and forecasts, handling cyber emergencies, coordinating incident response, and issuing information security guidelines and advisories.

properties.regulation_type: CERT-In Functions
CERT-In Functions

title: CERT-In - Power to Call for Information and Give Directions
clause_text: For carrying out the provisions of sub-section (4), the agency referred to in sub-section (1) may call for information and give direction to the service providers, intermediaries, data centres, body corporate and any other person.
plain_english_summary: CERT-In may call for information and give directions to service providers, intermediaries, data centres, body corporates, and any other persons for carrying out its cyber security functions.

title: CERT-In - Penalty for Non-Compliance with Directions
clause_text: Any service provider, intermediaries, data centres, body corporate or person who fails to provide the information called for or comply with the direction under sub-section (6), shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year or with fine which may extend to one lakh rupees or with both.
plain_english_summary: Failure to provide information or comply with CERT-In directions is punishable with imprisonment up to one year or a fine up to Rs 1 lakh, or both.

title: Penalty for Publishing False Electronic Signature Certificate
clause_text: No person shall publish a electronic signature Certificate or otherwise make it available to any other person with the knowledge that— (a) the Certifying Authority listed in the certificate has not issued it; or (b) the subscriber listed in the certificate has not accepted it; or (c) the certificate has been revoked or suspended, unless such publication is for the purpose of verifying a electronic signature created prior to such suspension or revocation. Any person who contravenes the provisions of sub-section (1) shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine which may extend to one lakh rupees, or with both.
plain_english_summary: Publishing or sharing an electronic signature certificate knowing it was not issued by the listed Certifying Authority, not accepted by the subscriber, or is revoked or suspended, is punishable with imprisonment up to two years or a fine up to Rs 1 lakh, or both.

title: Publication of Electronic Signature Certificate for Fraudulent Purpose
clause_text: Whoever knowingly creates, publishes or otherwise makes available a electronic signature Certificate for any fraudulent or unlawful purpose shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine which may extend to one lakh rupees, or with both.
plain_english_summary: Knowingly creating, publishing, or making available an electronic signature certificate for a fraudulent or unlawful purpose is punishable with imprisonment up to two years or a fine up to Rs 1 lakh, or both.

title: Confiscation
clause_text: Any computer, computer system, floppies, compact disks, tape drives or any other accessories related thereto, in respect of which any provision of this Act, rules, orders or regulations made thereunder has been or is being contravened, shall be liable to confiscation: Provided that where it is established to the satisfaction of the court adjudicating the confiscation that the person in whose possession, power or control of any such computer, computer system, floppies, compact disks, tape drives or any other accessories relating thereto is found is not responsible for the contravention of the provisions of this Act, the court may, instead of making an order for confiscation, make such other order authorised by this Act against the person contravening.
plain_english_summary: Computers, storage devices, and related accessories used in contravention of the Act are liable to confiscation, unless the possessor proves they were not responsible for the contravention.

title: Compensation, Penalties and Confiscation Not to Interfere with Other Punishment
clause_text: No compensation awarded, penalty imposed or confiscation made under this Act shall prevent the award of compensation or imposition of any other penalty or punishment under any other law for the time being in force.
plain_english_summary: Awards of compensation, penalties, or confiscations under this Act do not preclude other punishments or compensation under any other applicable law.

title: Application of the Act to Electronic Cheque and Truncated Cheque
clause_text: The provisions of this Act, for the time being in force, shall apply to, or in relation to, electronic cheques and the truncated cheques subject to such modifications and amendments as may be necessary for carrying out the purposes of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 by the Central Government, in consultation with the Reserve Bank of India, by notification in the Official Gazette.
plain_english_summary: The Act applies to electronic cheques and truncated cheques with such modifications as the Central Government may notify in consultation with the Reserve Bank of India.

title: Controller and Deputy Controller as Public Servants
clause_text: The Controller, the Deputy Controller and the Assistant Controllers shall be deemed to be public servants within the meaning of section 21 of the Indian Penal Code.
plain_english_summary: The Controller, Deputy Controller, and Assistant Controllers are deemed public servants under section 21 of the Indian Penal Code.

title: Power of Central Government to Give Directions to State Governments
clause_text: The Central Government may give directions to any State Government as to the carrying into execution in the State of any of the provisions of this Act or of any rule, regulation or order made thereunder.
plain_english_summary: The Central Government may issue directions to State Governments on implementing the provisions of the Act and rules made thereunder.

title: Removal of Difficulties
clause_text: If any difficulty arises in giving effect to the provisions of this Act, the Central Government may, by order published in the Official Gazette, make such provisions not inconsistent with the provisions of this Act as appear to it to be necessary or expedient for removing the difficulty: Provided that no order shall be made under this section after the expiry of a period of two years from the commencement of this Act.
plain_english_summary: The Central Government may make provisions to remove difficulties in implementing the Act by order published in the Official Gazette, but only within two years of the Act's commencement.

title: Power of Controller to Make Regulations
clause_text: The Controller may, after consultation with the Cyber Regulations Advisory Committee and with the previous approval of the Central Government, by notification in the Official Gazette, make regulations consistent with this Act and the rules made thereunder to carry out the purposes of this Act. Such regulations may provide for: maintenance of data base records of Certifying Authorities; conditions for recognition of foreign Certifying Authorities; terms and conditions for licence; standards to be observed by Certifying Authorities; manner of disclosure by Certifying Authorities; particulars for electronic signature certificate applications; and manner in which subscribers shall communicate private key compromise.
plain_english_summary: The Controller may make regulations covering Certifying Authority databases, foreign authority recognition, licensing conditions, disclosure standards, certificate application particulars, and private key compromise notification, after consulting the Advisory Committee and with Central Government approval.

title: Power of State Government to Make Rules
clause_text: The State Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, make rules to carry out the provisions of this Act. In particular, and without prejudice to the generality of the foregoing power, such rules may provide for all or any of the following matters, namely:— (a) the electronic form in which filing, issue, grant, receipt or payment shall be effected under sub-section (1) of section 6; (b) for matters specified in sub-section (2) of section 6.
plain_english_summary: State Governments may make rules to carry out the provisions of the Act, particularly for prescribing electronic forms for filings, grant of licences, and payments under section 6.

title: Electronic Signature or Electronic Authentication Techniques and Procedures
clause_text: The Second Schedule specifies the electronic signature or electronic authentication technique and procedure for the purposes of section 3A. The Central Government may by notification add to or omit any electronic signature or electronic authentication technique from the Second Schedule, provided that no technique shall be specified unless it is reliable.
plain_english_summary: The Second Schedule lists the approved electronic signature and authentication techniques for the purposes of section 3A. The Central Government may add or remove techniques from the Schedule by notification, subject to a reliability requirement.
